segments: "0 seconds Aptis Speaking - 50 plus useful example phrases from Aptis Tutor, the place to come for all things Aptis related."
"13 seconds It can be easy to go blank in an oral exam, to forget everything you wanted to say,"
"20 seconds so here's part one of 50 useful starter phrases to help you speak more fluently."
"27 seconds We've tried to cover all the typical areas that come up in the speaking test."
"33 seconds The idea is for you to complete the phrases with your own ideas, but we've included some examples"
"39 seconds to help you get started. We've also highlighted grammar structures. Remember you can use these"
"47 seconds phrases to start answering questions in any oral exam not just the Aptis test."
"56 seconds Talking about likes and dislikes. Try to use a variety of synonyms to express your likes"
"1 minute, 4 seconds and dislikes not just \"I like\" \"I don't like\". \"I like going to concerts\" \"I enjoy romantic songs\""
"1 minute, 16 seconds I dislike classical music...I don't enjoy cooking...I love walking on the beach... I"
"1 minute, 25 seconds adore seaside holidays. I hate really hot weather. I detest going to the dentist's. So here we've got"
"1 minute, 36 seconds the basic likes and dislikes and more extreme, I love... I hate... I adore... I detest..."
"1 minute, 45 seconds Other ways of expressing your likes are 'keen on' eg. I'm keen on cycling...I'm not keen on cycling."
"1 minute, 57 seconds I'm not a real fan of action films... I'm into spicy food..."
"2 minutes, 7 seconds As you can see all these expressions are followed by verb + ing plural nouns or uncountable nouns"
"2 minutes, 16 seconds in British English. In American English it's also common to use 'to + infinitive' eg 'I"
"2 minutes, 25 seconds like to cook', 'I like to walk on the beach' But in British English we use this structure"
"2 minutes, 33 seconds more for when we think 'something's a good idea' rather than to express likes. Eg"
"2 minutes, 41 seconds 'If I have a flight to catch I like to get to the airport two hours early'."
"2 minutes, 49 seconds I don't actually enjoy going to the airport two hours early but I think it's a good idea."
"2 minutes, 59 seconds But we always use 'to + infinitive' in British and American English after 'would like' or 'would love' I'd like to see you again I'd love to live in a hot country."
"3 minutes, 18 seconds If you use 'very much' remember it goes at the end of the sentence."
"3 minutes, 24 seconds 'I like driving very much' but it's more natural to use really I really like driving"
"3 minutes, 36 seconds Another way of expressing what you like or don't like is to use these phrases 'One of my favorite"
"3 minutes, 42 seconds / least favorite songs is Heroes' 'My favorite /least favorite film of all time is Blade Runner'"
"3 minutes, 57 seconds Or superlatives 'The best thing about my job / the worst thing about my job is having to get up early'"
"4 minutes, 10 seconds The thing I like least about my flat is its size."
"4 minutes, 18 seconds Talking about hobbies and ability. My hobbies are listening to music and swimming."
"4 minutes, 29 seconds I'm interested in health and fitness and doing sport. I'm really into horror films."
"4 minutes, 40 seconds We also talk about our abilities what you're good at/what you're bad at. I'm good at playing the guitar... I'm not very good at languages... I'm terrible at drawing..."
"4 minutes, 57 seconds Talking about the present routines and habits. Another typical question in the first part of the oral exam."
"5 minutes, 11 seconds They may ask what you usually do at weekends Etc I'm hardly ever bored..."
"5 minutes, 23 seconds I always go to the coast at weekends. Remember with the adverbs of frequency if"
"5 minutes, 32 seconds it's the verb 'to be' it goes first all the other verbs go after we adverb of frequency"
"5 minutes, 43 seconds Try to use a conditional to up the level a bit if 'I have some free time I usually watch my favorite series'"
"5 minutes, 54 seconds I always go to the beach if the weather's good."
"6 minutes 'We usually go abroad each year/ every year' These expressions go at the end of the sentence."
"6 minutes, 9 seconds We often go to the mountains once a year/ twice a year. Remember after"
"6 minutes, 15 seconds that three times four times five times a week a month a year Etc"
"6 minutes, 27 seconds Talking about the past and your experience is another very typical area in the oral exam."
"6 minutes, 36 seconds Remember that words the word 'ago' goes at the end of a sentence.'I worked in Germany six years ago'"
"6 minutes, 47 seconds Try to vary your past forms instead of just using the past simple use 'used to' eg"
"6 minutes, 53 seconds 'I used to play outside a lot when I was little we used to live in London'"
"7 minutes, 1 second Or you can use 'would' which is a synonym of 'used to' for activities but not for states of being,"
"7 minutes, 10 seconds so we can say 'I would play outside a lot' but we can't say 'We would live in London.'"
"7 minutes, 22 seconds 'I've never been abroad alone' 'We've traveled abroad many times' Here we're talking about 'experience' without specific dates and use the 'present perfect'"
"7 minutes, 33 seconds as you can see highlighted in blue. 'I've lived here for 10 years'... 'I've lived here since"
"7 minutes, 42 seconds 2012'.... Remember period of time + for with present perfect and a 'point in time' + since"
"7 minutes, 56 seconds Another useful way of talking about your experiences are these expressions 'I remember one particular time when I had a problem at work'"
"8 minutes, 9 seconds 'The most memorable occasion was my fifth birthday party' 'I can't remember the last time I read a book'"
"8 minutes, 18 seconds If you liked"
"8 minutes, 23 seconds this video then please subscribe to our Channel, leave a like, comment or question and we will"
"8 minutes, 29 seconds answer you as soon as we can. We have more information and practice here on our website www.aptistutor.com"
"8 minutes, 41 seconds Thanks"
